utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Good morning, ladies and gentlemen. Good morning to the interpreters and to the technical booth. Are you all ready to start? Thank you. Excuse me for this delay, but you know all too well the reasons for it, so we will try and maybe remedy that. We are going to continue with yesterday's witness, are we?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Yes, your Honours, we have the overnight witness who will be called to testify this morning.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: In that case, I will ask the Registrar to lower the blinds so that the witness can be shown in. Mr. Registrar, could you please call the case?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Case IT-95-14/1-T, the Prosecutor against Zlatko Aleksovski.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Niemann, could you please give us the appearances?

utterances.speaker: MR. NIEMANN
utterances.text: My name is Niemann. I appear with my colleagues, Mr. Meddegoda and Ms. Sutherland and Ms. Erasmus for the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you. And the Defence, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Good morning, your Honours. My name is Goran Mikulicic; along with my colleague Joka, we represent the accused, thank you. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Good morning, witness. Can you hear me well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can hear you well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: We are now going to continue to listen to your testimony. Yesterday you made a solemn declaration that you will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth. Are you prepared to do the same thing today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that is correct, the whole truth and nothing but the truth, that is correct.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Meddegoda, please proceed. WITNESS O (continued)

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Good morning, Witness O.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: When we adjourned last afternoon, you stated in evidence that you were arrested and brought to the Kaonik camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: And you also said that you were brought to a hangar building in that camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Could you tell this court what happened upon arrival in the hangar building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we were brought to the hangar building, we first got off the buses and entered the hangars, there were pallets that were arranged on the floor. We were quite a few in there. Then we were ordered to take everything out of our pockets, and we had to turn around facing the wall with our hands up. We were standing on these pallets. After a while, they searched us to assure themselves that we did not have any objects like knives or such in our pockets.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: By whom were you searched in the hangar building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: These were some HVO soldiers. They searched us. I do not know them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: How did you know they were HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had camouflage uniforms on, and the HVO insignia.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Were any camp officials present at the time you were brought to the hangar?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Mr. Aleksovski was present.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: And do you remember what Mr. Aleksovski was wearing at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think he was also wearing a camouflage uniform. He told us not to be afraid, that there was nothing to be afraid of, that we were safe here, that nothing would happen to us, and things proceeded in that way.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Do you remember what happened the next day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next day, we were called out, so that night we had spent there, then we were called out and we were taken to be used as human shields -- 20 of us were hauled out, 15 of us were tied up and five were returned to the hangar. A bus arrived. We were tied up, hands behind our backs, and Mr. Aleksovski was there. An HVO soldier tied us up -- the first one who came refused to do this, and then the second one came and tied us up. There was a white rope which he pulled out. He ordered us to turn around facing the wall of the hangar and then he tied us five together. After we were tied up, we were ordered to board the bus. When we climbed on to the bus, then the order was issued to drive in the direction that we were supposed to go to, that is, to go to Skradno. The bus brought us near to the bridge at Skradno and to the Vatrostalna factory. It could not go any further, so we got off the bus there, and we were lined up.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: What happened after you got off the bus and you were lined up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then they called on the villagers to surrender, using the loud speaker, and we were there for about half an hour and apparently the village surrendered. Then we were again boarded on to the bus, still tied up, and we went back to Kaonik. When --

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Now, witness, before you proceed any further, your Honours, may I ask the usher to show to the witness an aerial photograph, of which there are copies for your Honours and for Mr. Mikulicic.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is number 94. (Handed).

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Witness, could you please carefully look at the aerial photograph on the ELMO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: And tell this court the point to which you were taken from the camp -- the point near the bridge that you spoke of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is the place where we crossed the Kozica River.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Could you please point out the bridge?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here (indicates). This is the bridge. This is before the Vatrostalna factory. You cross here (indicating) to Sendolin Kuce, and that is where we stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Could you, using the highlighter behind you, could you mark the bridge at which you had to get off the bus. I want you to mark the bridge first, witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Ask him to circle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Could you circle the bridge that you spoke of in your testimony, witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness marked photograph).

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: That is the bridge. Using a different coloured marker, could you please mark the place at which you and the others were forced to stand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness marked photograph).

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: In which direction were you standing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Facing the village -- we were facing the village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Which village was that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was the village of Skradno.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: You said you were there for about half an hour, as far as you remember?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, maybe 40 minutes -- no more than one hour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: What happened thereafter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When those people surrendered, this whole thing was over, and then we boarded the bus again and we went towards Kaonik. At Kaonik, in front of the Tisovac store, which was a supermarket of sorts, the bus turned around. We got off and we went to Strane, again as human shields.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Witness, could you, again looking at the same photograph that is before you, which is Exhibit P94, could you point out the place at which you got off the bus and walked towards Strane you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Here is the spot where we got off -- this is where the store was (indicating) and there is also some kind of a warehouse there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Could you please circle that spot using a highlighter that is besides you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can -- red or blue?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Whatever colour that is there -- blue, please, yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness marked photograph).

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: You got off the bus at the point and you said this is where the shop is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: This is where we got off the bus, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: What happened after you got off the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were still tied up and the HVO soldiers took us to the intersection to Podjele and towards the old rail road station and post office and at this intersection, at this junction, we were also made to stand, lined up, and facing the village of Strane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Could you please, using the red coloured pen, mark the point at which you and the others were forced to stand facing the village of Strane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness marked photograph).

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: What happened when you were standing there facing Strane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We stood there for quite a while. A colleague of ours was sent there to ask them to surrender. As he was walking, they shot after him and so he ducked into cover, and the HVO soldiers also shot over our heads and we were ordered not to bend. I do not know who it was, but somebody from the forest off to the side was shooting, also, at us. There was a young man who had a sniper rifle and he was also shooting in the direction of the village of Strane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Do you know what happened at the village of Strane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After a while, when we were pulled back, I learned -- we heard, that is, from the HVO soldiers, that the village also surrendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: How long were you standing as a human shield facing the village of Strane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I cannot remember any more -- it could have been one hour or two -- at this point, I was only concerned whether I was going to survive or not, because the shooting started from behind us and then they also were shooting from the other side and we were specifically ordered not to bend, because, if we did bend, if we did duck, then we would be shot.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Thereafter, you were returned to the Kaonik camp, were you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we were returned on foot to the camp, because the distance is about a kilometre, maybe 0.8 kilometres to the hangar.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Do you remember being taken anywhere else the next day, the following day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, the next day, in the morning, some time around 10, 10.30, I was taken to Merdani. This was the third time that I was taken as a human shield.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: On this occasion, how many of you were taken to Merdani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Again, 15 persons were taken to Merdani.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: And before being taken, could you describe what happened to the prisoners before being taken? Were you tied --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, yes, yes, we were tied up the same way, just as the first and second time when I was used as a human shield -- both those locations, so this was the third time, but it was on the second day. We were also tied up, also hands behind our backs, also escorted by the HVO soldiers. We boarded the bus. The bus brought us from Kaonik to Podjele. That is where we got off and the bus went back, because the bus could not proceed any further. The road was bad and, also, the bridge was not strong enough to support the bus, so, at the bridge, we were abused, we were -- they cursed us, they threatened to throw us into the Kozica River, and then we proceeded from there. They still verbally abused us and cursed us, as they were taking us towards Merdani. From this junction towards Podjele, they proceeded for maybe another 300 metres further and then they lined us up facing the village of Merdani. They kept us there for about an hour, an hour and a half. Merdani refused to surrender and then they took us back. We went back on foot, all the way to the hangar, and, when we got there, we were already assigned for digging, this forest digging. However, I was taken to a cell. I was not taken back to the hangar. I saw that my colleagues, my fellow inmates, with whom I was in the hangar were no longer there. I later found they were taken to dig, and this is what then proceeded -- this scenario sort of was then repeated daily.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: May I give you an aerial photograph which I may wish to show you. Your Honours, may the usher be asked to place this photograph on the ELMO with copies to your Honours and to Mr. Mikulicic? (Handed).

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is document number 95.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Witness, could you carefully look at Exhibit 95 and, on that exhibit or that photograph, could you, using the pointer, point to the place where you were taken by bus -- where you had to get off the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I could not orient myself. This is where the bus brought us -- shall I mark it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Yes, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Shall I mark it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Yes, please, you may proceed to mark the place that the bus brought you to.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness marked photograph).

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: And from there you and the others had to get off the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: What happened after you got off the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then we came -- then we crossed the bridge and then that is where they were provoking us -- they verbally abused us, there were obscenities spoken there, and then we started towards Podjele.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Could you mark the place at which you and the others were forced to stand facing the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We who were tied up and lined up as human shields facing the village?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Yes, please. You may use a different colour marker, witness.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness marked photograph).

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: On that occasion, you were facing the village of Merdani, as you said?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, yes, facing the village of Merdani.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Witness, thereafter you said you were returned to the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: And you also said a while ago that thereafter you were taken to dig trenches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Do you remember where you were taken to to dig trenches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To Kula, towards -- in the direction of Busovaca and I was taken to Kula only once. I do not know why. After that, I was only in the cells -- I was never taken to dig again after that. I do not know why. I was beaten there by some soldier -- I do not know who it was -- and he beat me with a shovel over my back. In the evening, both myself and my fellow inmates were returned on a truck of the RAV make and after that we were brought back to the camp. After that I was never taken to dig again -- my fellow inmates were, but I myself was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Did you continue to be detained in the cell throughout your stay in the camp from the time you were transferred to the cell building?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, these 13 days until I was exchanged I spent there and my fellow inmates were changing, depending on who was taken to work, and the number also varied from 10, 15, to 20 and even 30 -- in a very small and confined space. When the inmate prisoners were coming back from this forced labour, they would receive one portion of food for two persons and they were exhausted, they were tired. Also, there were no hygienic conditions -- you could not wash, you could not shave. There was one stove in the building. There was a toilet, which was to the left of Mr. Aleksovski's office and this is how we were surviving that period of time, that is, the people who transferred from the hangar to the cells until we were exchanged. We could hear noises and shouts and people were being beaten -- those who were going to the front-lines and people were beaten up in the camp. Then, from the camp, I went back to Busovaca and proceeded from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: That was after you were exchanged in February?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: And you were exchanged on 8 February 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on the 8th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Witness, you remember earlier on you said when you arrived in the hangar in Kaonik you were met by Mr. Aleksovski?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Did you know Mr. Aleksovski from before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: How did you know him?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I knew him from Zenica, from the corrections centre there -- I knew he worked there and also he was in Vatrostalna for a while. He commuted and then later he got an apartment in Busovaca, so that is how I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: I tender Exhibits 93, 94 and 95. I have no further questions from this witness -- 93 was the document I tendered yesterday under seal, your Honours, and this morning I tendered two documents, 94 and 95.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Yes. They are going to be tendered and admitted. Do you have any further questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: No, I have no further questions in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you very much. In that case, Mr. Mikulicic, do you have questions for this witness, or Mr. Joka?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: May it please the court, Witness O, I would like to ask a few questions. Today, you told this Trial Chamber that you were used on two occasions as a human shield.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Not the two occasions -- on two different days, the first day was at Skradno and a different day at Merdani.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: You said you had information, or maybe I did not understand you well, but the village had surrendered; in that other case the village had not surrendered. Did you see Skradno and Strane surrender or did you only hear about it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we knew where the trenches were where we were digging from the other inmates. I know the village did not surrender.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: I asked you about Skradno?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It surrendered on that very day.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Did you see it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because they called them with a loud speaker.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Who did it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The person who brought us.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: How did you see people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: There were people that came down from the village of Skradno.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: And how about the village of Strane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They came, I do not know whether they surrendered but they came from the forest.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: And Merdani did not surrender?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, Merdani did not surrender, because I know it from other people who were there digging and they told me that Merdani had not surrendered.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Could you please tell the Trial Chamber how far you were from the village of Skradno while you were there -- how far away from you in metres, if you can say?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Do you mean from the Croat houses?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: No, no --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: May the counsel be advised to slow down the witness, please?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Where the Muslim houses were or the Croat houses.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Witness O, excuse me to interrupt you; could you please speak slowly, because, as you know, there are interpreters who have to translate. They cannot follow you if you speak too quickly. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: The first were Croat houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, they were first Croat houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Could you tell me how far away you were from the Croat houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 150 metres.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: And they came, the Muslim houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: How far were you from the Muslim houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: 500 metres, the first Muslim houses were 500 metres away.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Let us go to the village of Strane -- first you spoke of Skradno so Strane -- how far you were from the village of Strane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You know what, from the place where we were, there is the road Travnik/Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: You can tell us in metres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You cannot see the village completely, because you can see the woods and there is the old school that can be seen and a couple of Muslim houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: So the woods separated you from the village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was on the right-hand side from us.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Merdani, how far away were you from that village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: About 800 metres or 1 kilometre away.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Do you know whether, in Skradno, there were any BiH army members?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Do you know that at Strane there were any members of the BiH army?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Were there BiH army members there or not?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Could you please tell us, were you registered by an international organisation while you were at Kaonik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was registered by the Red Cross. I have got a document about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: When, how many days after?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Some six or seven days afterwards. Mr. Aleksovski was present when we were registered.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Tell me whether anybody from your family -- but please do not mention any names -- whether anybody was also deprived of liberty the same time you were?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All my family.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Even your father?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Was he also brought there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, but he was returned back home, because he was an elderly man and other older people were also returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Was it the same day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, but, your Honours, I only speak the truth. I do not need to tell any lies, so I only say what is true.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: You said that you knew Mr. Aleksovski from before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: You mentioned the correction centre in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I knew from those people who said that he was at the corrections centre.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Did you have anything to do with the corrections centre in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: You mentioned that the accused was given an apartment in Busovaca?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After the corrections centre when I went to Busovaca -- maybe Mr. Aleksovski does not remember -- we even had an occasion when we sat down in a cafe together.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: You heard something about his apartment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, because I heard something -- I would see him at Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: You concluded he was there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was my conclusion. On some occasions we sat down in a cafe together.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Witness O, could you please tell me, before the breakout of the conflict, what was your relationship with the Croat population -- you personally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: First of all, Sir, I never ever thought something like that would happen -- I never had any doubts. (redacted) (redacted) We were good to one another. We helped one another, and I have to say even today not everybody is extreme. Some people are very nice.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: You have some people you are on good terms with even today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, and I will always be on good terms with such people.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Did any Croats help you or save your property while you were at Kaonik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they did not -- my house was burned down.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: So your house was burned down?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it was burned down and somebody was repairing it when we got out.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: And your father's house and your brothers' houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, they are all right, nothing happened to them, but we are not allowed to go to those houses. When I go through Kacuni, Kiseljak and Stari Put, I never go through Busovaca.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Did you exchange your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Before you were arrested, did you own a vehicle?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Was this vehicle returned to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, all my property was taken away from me.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: After you were brought to Kaonik, were you released for a short moment to go home?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: To have a wash and bring some food?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Is it true?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Did you, from somebody who was at Kaonik, who was there in an official position, like one of the guards or an HVO member, receive any blankets?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, a young man brought a blanket to me and he gave me a loaf of bread.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Do you know his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not. I only know that he comes from a village from up there towards Ravno.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Oh, that is a different matter -- what I did -- it belongs to another matter, another trial, not this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: I am not asking you about another judicial matter, I am asking you what you did?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: What kind of a work duty is it -- could you explain that to the Trial Chamber?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, it can be any kind of obligation, it was forced labour.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Could you tell us what you did? I do not know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: So you were the person who did it?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there were five of us.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: So you were one of the persons who were collecting people around?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was collecting them around, so my fellow Muslims hated me for that. They cursed me all the time because of that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Only one question more. When you were telling us about the events concerning the human shields in two villages on the first day and on the following day in a third village, was anyone hurt?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Were there any injuries or any casualties?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there were not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I want to tell the truth -- nobody -- there were no casualties, nobody was injured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Meddegoda, have you got any additional questions.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: I have no questions in re-examination. I would wish to draw the attention of the court to three redactions in the testimony and in the course of cross-examination. That is at page 18, line 14, which need to be redacted, and at page 20, there is lines 19 and 20, and on page 21, line 14 and also page 22, line 13.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Registrar, I think that we have already done those and that Mr. Mikulicic has agreed. So, these parts of the transcript will be redacted. Mr. Meddegoda, have you completed your examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Yes. May I also point out two more redactions -- page 22, lines 13 and 19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Yes. We will do it. The dialogue was a very dynamic one. There were some references, yes. I will now ask my colleagues whether they have any questions for the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO NAVIA
utterances.text: Just a simple question. Was there any difference -- uniforms or insignia -- between guards and HVO soldiers?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They had the insignia -- I did not see the Croat army there -- I cannot say that I saw them, because I did not see them there. There were HVO insignia, and there were black uniforms, with no insignia at all. Those were the other two types of uniforms -- the other uniforms we could see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Witness O -- could the usher go to Witness O, because I would like to ask him a question about the map. This is Exhibit 95 that I would like to refer to. Could that be placed on the ELMO? Witness O, you have indicated to us the first occasion when you were taken very near a bridge. Could you use a pointer, please, and point to us where the bridge was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes (witness marked photograph) yes, at the spot here in blue. We cannot see the river, because of the trees -- we cannot see the river. It is after the place where blue colour is. It is towards Podjele.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Could you show us on the map where Skradno is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness indicates). All this is Skradno.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: When we go near the supermarket the second time around, could you please point to the supermarket where you went on the second occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, this is where I pointed to the shop and the warehouse (indicates).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you. Could you tell us where -- could you point to the direction of Strane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From Sendoline Kuce where the bridge is -- towards that direction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Could you point out the village on the map -- the village of Strane -- where is Strane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Near Skradno.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Is Strane on the map?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Indicates).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: So Strane is there. Thank you. Thank you very much, Witness O. This is the end of your testimony. The International Criminal Tribunal thanks you for coming and hopes you have a safe trip back home to your country?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Meddegoda, I think that we can use this occasion to make a small break before we start with the following witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Your Honours, I discovered another redaction which may have to be made which is in cross-examination. That is connected to the earlier one I mentioned -- the last one is at page 23, it is line 3 on page 23, and that is connected to line 19 on page 22, so for that reason I thought that line may need to be redacted as well, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Yes, we are going to redact that as well. We are now going to have a 15-minute break, because the next break will be 20 minutes long so that will allow us to have some lunch. (11.17am) (A short break) (11.38am)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: We are now going to work until 5 to 1. After that, we will have a 20-minute break, which means that we will start again at 13.15 until 14.30. This is to give you the framework, but we can alter that if necessary. Mr. Meddegoda, you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Thank you. The next Prosecution witness is witness number 8 in paragraph 4 of the Prosecution's inventory of witnesses dated 20 March. In respect of that witness I am seeking to make an application for protective measures in respect of Rule 35. I ask that your Honours give a pseudonym to this witness and the image of the witness's face be distorted during the course of his testimony. I have indicated this to my learned friend Mr. Mikulicic and I understand he has no objection to my application. In those circumstances, I move that your Honours be pleased to grant the protective measures I am seeking on behalf of that witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The Defence has no objection and we agree with the proposal made by the Prosecutor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mikulicic. The Trial Chamber will grant the measures requested, and we are going to take all the relevant action, which means lowering the blinds. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Good morning, Sir. Can you hear me?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I can.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Please now read the solemn declaration that the usher will give you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: You may be seated. Do you feel comfortable?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I feel well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: You are now going to answer the questions which Mr. Meddegoda is going to ask you. Witness P

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Their Honours have granted the protective measures you asked for. During the course of your testimony, do not refer to any details that would reveal your identity. You will be known as "Witness P", during the course of your testimony. Witness, could you please read the name that is written on this sheet of paper and confirm whether or not that name is yours (Handed).

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness nods head).

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO NAVIA
utterances.text: I did not hear if you said "yes" or "no"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness nods head).

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters cannot hear the witness.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: This is Exhibit 96.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: I tender it under seal. I would advise you to speak into the microphone. Witness P, you are Bosniak by ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Your religion is Islam?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Could you please state your age?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I am 44 years old.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Witness, I would like to take you back to the events of January 1993. Do you remember January 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I remember it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Do you remember when you were arrested in January 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that. It was in the second half of January -- somewhere towards the second half of January.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: You cannot remember the exact date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I do not remember the exact date, but between the 20th, 22nd or something like that -- I cannot recall exactly.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Who arrested you in the latter part of January 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was at home with my wife and my brother and his wife were there. We were sitting down at breakfast -- that was on the upper floor. Somebody knocked at the door and I went downstairs to see who it was. When I opened the door, I saw a man wearing a camouflage uniform, who told me to get out. I went outside and I saw there were four or five soldiers standing there also wearing camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Did you happen to know who this man was who knocked on your door?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I knew those men. They were HVO soldiers. I knew one of those five or six soldiers.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Did you know him personally?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I knew him personally.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Do you remember his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I do. His surname is Babic, and his nickname is Nikesa.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: You said you went outside and you saw four or five soldiers standing outside. What were those soldiers dressed in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were wearing camouflage uniforms and they were armed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Do you know to which army they belonged?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the HVO.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: What happened when you went out of your house?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went out of the house and then the person whom I saw, Niko, when I opened the door, he asked me whether anybody else was in the house. I said my brother was in there. He sent another soldier to fetch him. My brother went downstairs. I said, "Maybe we should get dressed." He said, "You do not need anything. You are going for an interrogation." Then he asked the soldier to take us to the petrol station

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we went out, there might have been some 10 people there, all of them civilians.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: What happened thereafter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I understood that that was some kind of a collection place -- they were collecting us -- there were maybe 30 of us. Then a bus came and they took us to Kaonik in the hangar there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Do you remember what happened the next day after you were brought to Kaonik?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The next day, once we spent the night there, it was between breakfast and lunch -- the doors of the hangar opened and an HVO soldier came in, and he showed like this with his hand (indicating). He counted 15 people and told us to go outside. When we did so, he lined us up and asked us whether anyone knows how to tie up. We did not know what -- we were not aware that we were going to tie ourselves up. We all were silent and nobody knew how to tie up. Then, one of the HVO soldiers took a rope and tied us up in three groups of five. One of their officers took down our names and then we boarded the bus. The bus took us across the Kozica River towards Merdani, and --

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: What happened when you were taken towards Merdani?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were taken there -- part of the journey we did by bus and the rest of it on foot. We arrived at a place where they ordered us to stop. We did so and we were there for about two to three hours and then we knew that -- one of the HVO soldiers told us that we were now the human shield and that one of ours went to negotiate with the villagers of Merdani, either for them to surrender or for them to surrender their arms or weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: I hand this aerial photograph to the witness. There is a copy for the court as well as for Mr. Mikulicic. I tender that document as the next exhibit in order.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It is Exhibit 97. (Handed).

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Witness, you said a while ago that you were taken to a point by bus. Could you please carefully look at the aerial photograph that is on the ELMO and, using the pointer, could you please point to the place where you were taken by bus and where you had to get off the bus? Could you please look at the photograph that is on the ELMO -- the aerial photograph? I suggest you look at the photograph that is on the ELMO beside you and then point out on that and not on the map -- on the screen. You may take your time, witness, with the photograph. You may leave it if you cannot find on that map the place in Merdani that you were taken to. Witness, what is the place that you pointed out?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Would you please ask the witness to speak up?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Could you please speak into the microphone. Witness, could you please speak up to the microphone?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They brought us to a place where there were only two houses -- this road was leading to a village up there, but I do not know the name of the village (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Is that the place that you had to get off the bus. Could you please first point out the place at which you and the others had to get off the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness indicates on photograph).

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Could you circle that place using a highlighter that is beside you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness marks photograph with red highlighter).

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: What happened from there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We got off the bus and then we went on foot for about this length (indicating) and then we arrived -- I cannot see the houses where we arrived to, but roughly speaking thereabouts (indicating).

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: What did you have to do when you arrived there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we arrived there, we stopped -- we walked there and then we stopped. We did not do anything. They went towards those houses and we heard that they were talking. They were discussing, talking, and there was a guard there who guarded us and all the others went to the houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: What happened thereafter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were there for some two to three hours and then the person who went to negotiate with the Merdani villagers, he had gone away and that he would not return, and so they were angry and they were cursing. We were afraid, because we heard the noise and the curses and we did not know what would happen to us. We said, in case somebody from our side starts shooting from Merdani, probably it might -- something might happen to us, we might be killed. So they were angry and ordered us to turn around, and we went on foot to the bridge. When we reached the bridge over the Kozica River, one of the soldiers told us to stop and we stopped in the middle of the bridge. I was in the middle row -- there were three rows, so I was in the middle row and one of the soldiers from the left bank of Kozica started going towards us. Those who were in the first row -- tied up in the first row -- I was in the middle row -- he came from the left-hand side -- and when he came to me, I was wearing a jacket -- a camouflage jacket, which was given to me by an HVO soldier, and on the left arm, the left sleeve, there was an HVO insignia. When he saw that, he could not understand why I was there, if I was one of their soldiers. Then he concluded that I could certainly not be one of their soldiers and he cursed me, and then he took a knife and I was really very terrified at that moment. My hands were tied up and I was looking through the holes of the bridge to the river and I could see myself already dead. I was really very scared. He took the knife and he started taking the HVO insignia off. When he did that, he went to the third line and he also mistreated -- abused them as well. That all might have lasted for some 10 minutes. After that, they told us to move, but I could not move, because my legs would not move, and so then we started again on foot and we came to the cells in the camp. We were untied and we went inside and sat at a table, but our hands -- we sat down to eat, but as our hands had been tied up for a long time, I could not even hold anything to eat with. My arms were so numb.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Witness, before you were returned to the camp, you said you were to stand facing a village. Which village were you facing when you and the others were standing -- in the direction of which village were you facing -- what is the name of the village in the direction of which you were standing?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In the direction of the village of Merdani.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: You said you were returned to the camp and you were returned to the building with the cells; is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: For how long -- how many days did you spend in the cell?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Only spent one day in the hangar where there were no cells -- the rest of the time I was in the building where the cells were, and I also spent an additional day in another hangar where there were no cells, so I spent two nights in total in two different hangars and the rest in the cell.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Witness, do you remember when you were released from prison -- from the Kaonik camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Of course I remember. This is like my second birthday. It was on the 8th -- do you mean where it was?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: No, when was that, sorry?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 8 February.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: After release, where did you go to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to Zenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Witness, during the period that you spent in the camp, did you happen to see the camp commander?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, on one occasion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Would you be able to recognise the camp commander if you saw him again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Witness, could you please look around this court and say whether the camp commander whom you saw in the prison is present in court today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Could you point out the direction in which he is in this court?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness points to his left in the direction of the accused).

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: I would wish to point out a redaction which has to be made in the evidence. On

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: 32, lines 1 and 2. I have no further questions in chief.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It has been redacted.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Witness P, you have answered the questions of the Prosecutor. Mr. Mikulicic, Mr. Joka, you are now going to proceed to cross-examination. Witness, you are going to answer Mr. Joka's questions on behalf of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honours. Please tell the Trial Chamber whether you have ever been convicted before?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, never.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Can you tell us what type of school you finished?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: How many years?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Three years -- three.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: This is the elementary school plus three or all together three?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, elementary plus three -- three years of the secondary school.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: I am going to ask you, Mr. P, questions regarding the events when you were, as you call it, a human shield. This was in Merdani. Whose village was it; in other words, who lived there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: It was a Muslim village.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Was it an exclusively Muslim village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, exclusively.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: You told the Trial Chamber that you stood there for about two or three hours?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: You said, if I remember correctly, that you were told that you were a human shield?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Who told you this?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was told -- actually, I was not told directly, but the bus driver told all of us who were on the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: From the position where you were standing, how far was the village -- what was the distance in metres?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Which village?

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: The village you were standing facing.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe about two kilometres.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Excuse me, I did not hear you well?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: In a straight line, maybe it was about one kilometre. A straight line, one kilometre.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: In real terms?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe a little bit more.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Do you know whether this village was armed?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I did not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Do you know whether, in this village, there were any BiH army members?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know that.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Do you know, how was the front-line defined in this area?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Out of the 15 of you that were there, those 15 human shields, was anyone injured?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: You mean while --

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: While you were standing there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, no-one was injured.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Was there any shooting while you were standing there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, there was no shooting where we were, but we could hear.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: No, no, I am interested in where you were.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not where we were.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: You told the Trial Chamber about the incident with the soldier who noticed that you had a military top. Can you tell us who gave you this jacket?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When I arrived in the bus, from the bus station -- this was on the first day -- and this soldier of theirs, the HVO soldiers brought us there, so we got off the bus and, since I only had my jeans on and a sweater the bus driver asked me whether I was cold and I told him I was. He said, "Shall I give you my jacket?" I said, "Sure, why not." He said, "Will this patch bother you?" I said, "No, why, because I was cold."

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Do you know the driver's name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: What is his name?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: His name is Zeljko Oreskovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Does he have a nickname?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, "Bubreg", which means "kidney".

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Was this the same bus driver who took you there to be a human shield?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: And he gave you this jacket before you became a human shield?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: And he is the person that told you that you were going to be taken there as human shields?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: If I understand you correctly, you were a human shield wearing an HVO camouflage top?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Just one additional clarification, please. In your statement today, you said that 15 of you were placed in a position and that the military went ahead of you to negotiate?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, that is not what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Then I misunderstood you, could you please clarify?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When we arrived at the location -- how shall I put it -- where we should have been, one of the soldiers stayed with us. There were two or three houses there and the HVO soldiers were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: So where did they go -- to the left or the right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To the right, to the right.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: To those two houses.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Whose houses were these?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know whose houses they were.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Were they Muslim or Croat houses?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: They were not Croat, I think they could have been Serb. I had never been there before. I was never in that area.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: So those were not houses belonging to the village of Merdani because Merdani was further away?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, that was much further away -- a kilometre away.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Were you registered in Kaonik by any international organisation?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By the Red Cross.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: When was this; that is, how many days after your arrival there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I believe I cannot be specific, but let us say six or seven days.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Were you ever taken to dig trenches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was not.

utterances.speaker: MR. JOKA
utterances.text: Your Honours, no further questions of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Meddegoda, have you got any additional questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Nothing, your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO NAVIA
utterances.text: I am going to read some lines of the statement you signed only a few days ago: "I was informed by somebody of the guards that the commander of the camp was Zlatko Aleksovski. I did not know him from before and I saw him only once in the camp. I can describe him as a short man with a round face, blond hair. He seemed to me to be 40 years." Is that man in this room?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, he is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO NAVIA
utterances.text: Where?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness indicates with hand to his left) he is to the left of me in the back.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO NAVIA
utterances.text: Does he have blond hair?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, not the blond one -- the one to the left.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO NAVIA
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Witness P, the place you were taken to, you mentioned two houses, is that true -- is that correct -- you mentioned there were two houses. Do you recall that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: There was a discussion whether these houses belonged to Muslims, Croats or Serbs. How can you know or recognise whether a house is Muslim, Croat or Serb? Is there anything that enables you to recognise those houses and differentiate them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For instance, you can recognise them by the roofs -- you can recognise whether it is Croat, Serb or Muslim, but I do not recall the roofs of those two houses, but I know that this area was either Serb or Croat. It definitely was not Muslim.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness P. You have just completed your testimony. The International Criminal Tribunal thanks you for coming here and wishes you a safe return to your country. (The witness withdrew)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Meddegoda, the next witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Your Honours, the next Prosecution witness is witness number 9 at paragraph 4 of the inventory dated 20 March. I am seeking to make a similar application on behalf of this witness as well. The witness has sought protective measures, has sought that a pseudonym be assigned in the course of his testimony and also the image of his face be distorted during the course of his testimony. I have indicated this to my learned friend Mr. Mikulicic, and I understand he has no objection to the Prosecution's application.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Mr. Mikulicic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: The Defence has no objections, your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: In that case, we will adopt the same measures as for the previous witness. Please show the witness in. (The witness entered court)

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Good morning, Sir. Can you hear me? You will now read the solemn declaration, which the usher will hand to you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: You may be seated. Do you feel comfortable?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: You are now going to answer questions which Mr. Meddegoda, the Prosecutor, will ask you. WITNESS Q

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Witness, their Honours have been pleased to grant you the protective measures which you have requested. I would therefore advise you not to refer to any details that would reveal your personal identity, and I would now hand over to you a sheet of paper, which I ask you to look at and confirm whether your name appears on that sheet of paper or not. (Handed).

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: I tender that under seal.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Exhibit 98.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Witness, you are Bosniak by ethnicity?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Your religion is Islam?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, it is.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Would you state what your age is, witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Witness, I should have advised you that you will be known as Witness Q, and both the Prosecution, the Defence and the court will refer to you as Witness Q in the course of these proceedings. Witness Q, do you remember the events of January 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Do you remember when you were arrested in January 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was arrested on 25 January 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Where were you at the time you were arrested?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was in the centre of town.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Who arrested you on 25 January 1993?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The HVO military.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: What happened after being arrested by the HVO?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was placed on a bus and we were taken to the Kaonik camp, which was the former barracks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Where, in Kaonik camp, were you brought to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was brought to this former JNA barracks -- the former army -- at Kaonik.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: What type of a building was it that you were brought to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Those were some kind of hangars.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Do you remember being taken out of that hangar building the next day?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes. The next day I was taken out of the hangar and we were tied up -- we were bound, five of us together, and we were taken to be used as human shields.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Do you know -- how many of you were tied up to be taken as human shields?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All together, 15, but five were tied up with a single rope.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Is it only five persons who were tied up, or all 15 who were tied?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: All 15.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: After being tied up, where were you taken to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were taken in the direction of the village of Skradno.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE VOHRAH
utterances.text: Could you elicit from the witness the manner in which these people were tied up?

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Witness, could you tell this court how you were tied up -- in what form you were tied up?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Our hands were tied behind our backs.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Were you all tied together?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we were all tied together.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: How many were tied together -- were you tied together all 15 in one group or how were you tied?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, we were tied five together -- three groups of five.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Very well. You said, having been tied, you were taken to Skradno?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Where in Skradno were you taken to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: When you turn off from the main road towards Skradno, that is where we were taken. There is a bridge there, which crosses the river and continues in the direction of Skradno.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: And at what point did you have -- at any point did you have to get off the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We got off the bus.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: What happened having got off the bus?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were tied up, we got off the bus, and we were put in some kind of rows, five by five -- there were five of us tied together, so we were put in rows, facing one another.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Did you have to cross the bridge that you spoke of -- cross the river that you spoke of?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, we crossed the bridge -- some 10 or 15 metres on the bridge.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: What happened thereafter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We stood there for some 15 minutes. After that, a man, unknown to me, came and he stopped that operation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Then what happened after that operation was stopped?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We returned to the buses again, and we were driven towards the village of Strane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Witness, before we go to Strane, you said before the operation was stopped, you said you were standing in rows. In which direction were you facing when you were standing in rows?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were facing towards Skradno.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Sorry, I was referring to Skradno. It was after that that you were taken back to the bus. What happened thereafter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that, we went in the direction of the village of Strane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: How did you go in the direction of the village of Strane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Then, when we were driven there, we got off the buses again, and we were lined up in such a way so that all the 15 of us were in one row. We were lined up side by side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: When you were lined up, which direction were you facing on this occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were facing towards Strane -- the village of Strane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: What happened when you were lined up facing the village of Strane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The HVO soldiers stood right behind us and told us to go towards Strane.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: How many HVO soldiers were there standing behind you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Maybe some 10 or 15 of them -- I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Do you recall what happened thereafter?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: After that, a bullet passed by us and normally we bent towards the ground. An HVO soldier said that we should not do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: How long were you standing there for?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For some 30 to 40 minutes, all in all.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Do you know what happened in the village of Strane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know what had happened exactly. What I heard -- a man from the camp had been sent to Strane to negotiate with our people. I think that he succeeded in that, because we were withdrawn from there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Whom do you mean by "our people"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: From the camp -- a man from the camp, who was with us in the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: You said had been sent to negotiate with other people; whom do you mean by referring to "other people"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The people from the village -- the Muslims, the Bosniaks.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: What was the ethnic composition of the village -- are you aware of the ethnic composition of that village?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think the majority was Muslim.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: What happened thereafter, witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The HVO soldier had stopped that operation again and we were returned.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Where were you returned to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were returned to the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Whilst being detained in the camp, were you taken out for any other labour detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I was taken out to dig trenches.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Where were you taken to to dig trenches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was taken to the villages of Kula and Prosije.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: About how many times were you taken to Kula?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I think on two times.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: How were you taken to Kula -- by what means of transport?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: By a lorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: What did you have to do in Kula, on the first occasion?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We dug trenches and dugouts.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: On both occasions did you have to dig trenches and dugouts?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Whilst digging in Kula, were you ever mistreated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Could you tell this court what happened to you -- how you were mistreated?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: We were mistreated in all kinds of ways. That depended on the guards and how they felt. They would beat us with hands and feet, with rifle butts, with agricultural utensils and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Were you personally beaten in Kula?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Could you tell this court how you were beaten whilst digging in Kula?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I was also beaten with hands and feet and, also, with a pole -- handle.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Were you taken elsewhere to dig trenches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, to Prosije.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: How many times were you taken to Prosije to dig trenches?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Once.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Whilst you were detained in the camp, witness, did you have the occasion to see who the commander of the camp was?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: When did you first see him during your period of detention?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: The first time I saw him was when we arrived at the camp.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: What was he dressed in when you arrived in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: He was wearing a camouflage uniform.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Were there others -- apart from the camp commander, were there other camp officials present when you first arrived in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I do not know exactly, but I know there were other HVO soldiers there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: What were those HVO soldiers dressed in?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Also in camouflage uniforms.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Would you be able to recognise the camp commander if you see him again?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes, I would.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Witness, could you please look around this court and say whether the camp commander whom you saw in the Kaonik camp when you first arrived is present in court today?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Could you please point out the direction in which he is?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: (Witness points to his left in the direction of the accused).

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Was that the only occasion on which you said you saw the camp commander, when you arrived in the camp -- was that the only occasion on which you saw him in the camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: No, I saw him after that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Witness, for how long were you in Kaonik camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: For 14 or 15 days.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Do you know when you were released from Kaonik camp?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: On 8 February 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: Upon your release, where did you go?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: I went to Kacuni.

utterances.speaker: MR. MEDDEGODA
utterances.text: I have no further questions in chief.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE RODRIGUES
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Meddegoda. Mr. Mikulicic, have you got any questions to ask the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. MIKULICIC
utterances.text: Thank you, your Honour. Witness Q, I am Goran Mikulicic and I am Defence counsel to the accused in this matter. I will ask you a few questions. Could you please answer to the best of your recollection. You told us that you were arrested and brought to Kaonik.
